```{python}
#| tags: [parameters]

# The day folder on S3. DuckDB reads it directly, no download step.
EVENTS = "s3://436c-2026w1-weather/gdelt/events-daily/day=*/part.parquet"
DAYS = 7           # size of the window, in days back from the latest day on S3
TOP_COUNTRIES = 15 # bars in the country chart
TONE_COUNTRIES = 6 # lines in the tone chart
```

```{python}
#| output: false

import time
import duckdb
import pandas as pd
import plotly.express as px
import plotly.io as pio
from IPython.display import Markdown

NAVY, AMBER, GREEN, PAPER = "#002145", "#f2b134", "#2b7a3c", "#fbf9f4"

# Quarto's Jupyter engine shows the value of every expression in a cell, so a bare
# fig.update_layout(...) would draw a second copy of the chart. One output per cell.
get_ipython().ast_node_interactivity = "last_expr"

con = duckdb.connect()
con.execute("CREATE SECRET (TYPE s3, PROVIDER credential_chain, REGION 'ca-central-1')")
con.execute(f"CREATE VIEW events AS SELECT * FROM read_parquet('{EVENTS}', hive_partitioning => true)")

elapsed, queries = 0.0, 0

def q(sql: str) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Run a query against S3 and keep score of how long we spent in DuckDB."""
    global elapsed, queries
    t0 = time.perf_counter()
    df = con.execute(sql).df()
    elapsed += time.perf_counter() - t0
    queries += 1
    return df

# The window: the last DAYS days present on S3. Each file holds one day, and its
# own Day column carries the same date as the day= folder, so filtering on Day
# lets DuckDB skip whole files -- the point of the hive layout.
bounds = q(f"""
    SELECT max(Day) AS last_day, max(Day) - INTERVAL {DAYS - 1} DAY AS first_day
    FROM events
""").iloc[0]
WINDOW = f"Day BETWEEN DATE '{bounds.first_day:%Y-%m-%d}' AND DATE '{bounds.last_day:%Y-%m-%d}'"

totals = q(f"""
    SELECT count(*) AS rows_scanned, count(DISTINCT Day) AS days
    FROM events WHERE {WINDOW}
""").iloc[0]
```

```{python}
#| output: false

per_hour = q(f"""
    SELECT date_trunc('hour', strptime(DATEADDED, '%Y%m%d%H%M%S')) AS hour,
           count(*) AS events
    FROM events WHERE {WINDOW}
    GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1
""")

top_countries = q(f"""
    SELECT ActionGeo_CountryCode AS country, count(*) AS events
    FROM events
    WHERE {WINDOW} AND ActionGeo_CountryCode IS NOT NULL AND ActionGeo_CountryCode <> ''
    GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY events DESC LIMIT {TOP_COUNTRIES}
""")

leaders = "', '".join(top_countries.country.head(TONE_COUNTRIES))
tone = q(f"""
    SELECT Day AS day, ActionGeo_CountryCode AS country, avg(AvgTone) AS tone
    FROM events
    WHERE {WINDOW} AND ActionGeo_CountryCode IN ('{leaders}')
    GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY 1
""")

QUAD = {1: "verbal coop", 2: "material coop",
        3: "verbal conflict", 4: "material conflict"}
quad = q(f"""
    SELECT Day AS day, QuadClass, count(*) AS events
    FROM events WHERE {WINDOW}
    GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY 1, 2
""")
quad["class"] = quad.QuadClass.map(QUAD)
quad["share"] = quad.events / quad.groupby("day").events.transform("sum")

# Plotly draws every figure through the notebook renderer, which hardcodes a
# MathJax <script> tag. embed-resources would then inline a 2 MB copy of MathJax
# per chart. No chart here has math in it, so we turn that tag off.
pio.renderers.default = "notebook"
_to_html = pio.to_html
pio.to_html = lambda *a, **kw: _to_html(*a, **{**kw, "include_mathjax": False})

pio.templates["c436"] = pio.templates["plotly_white"]
pio.templates["c436"].layout.update(
    font=dict(family="Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif", color=NAVY, size=13),
    paper_bgcolor=PAPER, plot_bgcolor="white",
    colorway=[NAVY, AMBER, GREEN, "#6b8fae", "#b8860b", "#7fa88a"],
    margin=dict(l=56, r=24, t=28, b=64),
    legend=dict(orientation="h", title_text="", x=0, y=-0.26,
                yanchor="top", font_size=11, entrywidthmode="fraction"),
)
pio.templates.default = "c436"
```

## Row {height="40%"}

```{python}
#| title: Events per hour
fig = px.area(per_hour, x="hour", y="events")
fig.update_traces(line_color=NAVY, fillcolor="rgba(0,33,69,0.12)")
fig.update_layout(xaxis_title=None, yaxis_title="events")
fig
```

```{python}
#| title: Top countries by event count
fig = px.bar(top_countries.sort_values("events"), x="events", y="country",
             orientation="h")
fig.update_traces(marker_color=NAVY)
# tickmode linear keeps every country label, which Plotly otherwise thins out
fig.update_layout(xaxis_title="events", yaxis_title=None,
                  yaxis=dict(tickmode="linear", dtick=1, tickfont_size=11))
fig
```

## Row {height="40%"}

```{python}
#| title: Average tone by day
fig = px.line(tone, x="day", y="tone", color="country", markers=True)
fig.add_hline(y=0, line_dash="dot", line_color=NAVY, opacity=0.4)
# px puts the colour column's name on the legend, and horizontal entries collide
# unless each one is given a share of the width.
fig.update_layout(xaxis_title=None, yaxis_title="average tone",
                  legend_title_text="", legend_entrywidth=0.9 / TONE_COUNTRIES)
fig
```

```{python}
#| title: QuadClass mix per day
fig = px.bar(quad, x="day", y="share", color="class",
             category_orders={"class": list(QUAD.values())},
             color_discrete_sequence=[GREEN, "#7fa88a", AMBER, "#b03a2e"])
fig.update_layout(barmode="stack", xaxis_title=None, yaxis_title="share of events",
                  yaxis_tickformat=".0%",
                  legend_title_text="", legend_entrywidth=0.22)
fig
```

    f"{totals.rows_scanned:,}-row window, about {totals.rows_scanned * queries:,} "

)
